title: Competing risks: a correct hazard ratio, a wrong cumulative incidence
question: When population adjustment transports a time-to-event outcome with a competing cause, does a correctly transported cause-specific hazard ratio give the right cumulative incidence in the target, and what repairs it?
design: Anchored transport with exponential cause-specific hazards, the target's competing hazard differing from the source's beyond the measured covariate; 16 cells crossing that difference, effect modification and overlap; MAIC, cause-specific STC and STC with the competing hazard recalibrated to the target's reported competing-event proportion. 1000 replicates per cell.
answer: For competing risks, population adjustment transports the cause-specific hazard ratio (unbiased in every scenario) but not the cumulative incidence a decision model uses: when the target's competing hazard differed from the source's beyond the measured covariate, A's absolute incidence at 2 years was biased by up to 0.20 (true value 0.25) with coverage near zero. The between-arm difference was affected less. Recalibrating the competing hazard to the target's reported competing-event proportion removed the bias. The registered rule (bias beyond 0.05 wherever the competing hazard differed) was met in 20 of 24 method-scenarios; the exceptions were at half the competing hazard, with bias 0.041 to 0.049.
findings: Cause-1 log hazard ratio: bias within 3 MCSE in 16 of 16 scenarios, at most 0.013.

A's cumulative incidence from MAIC or STC: bias 0.13 to 0.20 with coverage at most 0.03 at four times the competing hazard; -0.04 to -0.06 at half; registered verdict NOT CONFIRMED (20 of 24 method-scenarios beyond 0.05).
Recalibrated competing hazard: bias at most 0.004; coverage 0.851 to 0.943 for the absolute incidence and 0.943 to 0.972 for the difference.
not_answered: Only the competing-risks family; cure fractions, recurrent events, ordinal and joint net-benefit outcomes not run. Exponential hazards, one covariate, no ML-NMR. Peer review has not been done.
estimand: Target cumulative incidence of the event of interest at 2 years under A, and its A-minus-C difference; cause-1 log hazard ratio
methods_compared: cause-specific STC with the competing hazard recalibrated to target data
